prize_parts.citation: For developing targeted protein degradation by heterobifunctional PROTACs and molecular glues that redirect the ubiquitin-proteasome system

statement.case_for: Targeted protein degradation turns a cellular process into a designable chemical reaction: a small molecule brings an E3 ligase and a chosen target together so that the target is destroyed rather than inhibited. That is a new modality with modular recognition design, and it has reached targets once called undruggable. Seven of eight members put it in their top four, and I rank it first because it changed what chemists and clinicians can do, from the PROTAC concept (Crews, Deshaies) to the mechanistic explanation of thalidomide-class glues through cereblon (Handa). Many independent laboratories reproduce the ternary-complex mechanism, and glue degraders are already approved drugs.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC has yet been approved, so the clinical proof for the heterobifunctional arm is still pending, and a prize now may look early. The prize also bundles two lines, PROTACs and glues, that could be argued as separate discoveries. The three-person limit forces a hard exclusion: Ciulli, Gray, Sakamoto and Kim all made decisive contributions, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures are arguably as central as Deshaies's early role.

responses.point: Peter ranks PROTACs fourth because approved PROTAC drugs are lacking and clinical validation is incomplete, and he suggests the PROTAC and glue arms may need separate recognition.
responses.response: I take the maturity worry seriously, but I do not think the chemical principle depends on a drug approval. Induced-proximity ubiquitination is established by ternary-complex structure and kinetics, which is the physically measurable standard you value, and lenalidomide-class glues acting through cereblon are already approved. Handa's cereblon work is the link that joins the two arms into one principle, so I would credit them together. I do disagree that Gray and Winkler (B028) should lead: it is a deep, mature piece of physical chemistry, but it has changed far less of what researchers and clinicians can do now.

responses.point: Heiner ranks sequencing by synthesis first as a measurable chemical invention that reshaped biology, and he sees PROTAC recognition as somewhat early on the therapeutic side.
responses.response: Sequencing by synthesis is a very strong, overdue candidate, and I would put it high on my list as well. I still prefer PROTACs because they open a new design space rather than a measurement capability, and the concept is validated across many labs and several clinical programmes. I accept the clinical caveat. My real reservation about B067 is the contested lineage between Solexa, 454 and others, which makes a clean prize harder than the Balasubramanian-Klenerman core suggests. I am open to being persuaded if the committee thinks that attribution is clean enough.

responses.point: Emma ranks condensates first as a general physical-chemical principle, and ranks ionizable lipid nanoparticles second while worrying about overlap with the 2023 Medicine prize and the contested credit among academic and industrial inventors.
responses.response: On lipid nanoparticles I agree about the attribution tangle, but I think the 2023 overlap is smaller than you fear: the Medicine prize covered nucleoside modification of the mRNA, while ionizable-lipid self-assembly and endosomal release are distinct chemistry. I would still need a clean three-name set, and I am less sure than you that Anderson should replace Hope or Madden. On condensates I respect the principle, but the in vivo evidence is contested and some of it is overexpression artefact. I see that as still maturing, whereas degraders are mechanistically settled.

responses.point: Andrei also ranks PROTACs first, but for base editing he would credit only David Liu, and he raises the overlap with the 2020 CRISPR prize.
responses.response: I agree on PROTACs and I find a Liu-only base-editing prize easier to defend than a trio, since Komor and Gaudelli did the decisive experiments in his laboratory. That is why I keep base editing as an alternative rather than a preferred part. The clinical data are thinner than for the lipid nanoparticle chemistry, and it sits close to a 2020 prize, so I would not combine it with PROTACs now.

uncertainties: Whether Ciulli should displace Deshaies or Handa as the third laureate.
Whether the PROTAC and molecular-glue arms should be recognised in one citation or split.
I rely on memory for the current clinical status of PROTACs and have not verified it.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile: I have no recorded tie to Crews, Deshaies, Handa or Ciulli. My peptide-nanoparticle and biosensor work is distant from this field; my postdoc mentors Molly Stevens and Freddy Boey are not credited here.
